articles.headline: President Trump criticizes 76ers' LeBron James for actions amid national anthem
articles.description: President Donald Trump has accused LeBron James of disrespecting the U.S. after the 76ers star appeared to continue his warmups during the national anthem.
articles.headlineJa: トランプ大統領、国歌演奏中の行動について76ersのレブロン・ジェームズを批判
articles.descriptionJa: ドナルド・トランプ大統領は、76ersのスター選手であるレブロン・ジェームズが国歌演奏中にウォーミングアップを続けていたように見えたとして、米国を軽視していると非難した。
articles.body:
President Donald Trump on Thursday accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the 76ers star appeared to continue his warmups while the national anthem was performed before Philadelphia's season opener Tuesday against the Knicks in New York.

James appeared to practice a golf swing and jump shot during The Star-Spangled Banner at Madison Square Garden. James, in his debut for the 76ers, was lined up alongside teammates who mostly stood still during the anthem.

"I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump said of James in a social media post sharing the video. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!"

Representatives for the 41-year-old James did not respond to requests for comment from ESPN. James, in his record 24th NBA season, was set to make his home debut for the Sixers on Thursday night against Cleveland.

Trump and James have been critical of each other for years, occasionally trading public swipes. 

Trump himself also has been criticized for his actions during the national anthem. In 2020, the Miami Herald posted a video of Trump waving his hands as if to conduct an orchestra while the national anthem was played at a Super Bowl watch party. In the brief video clip, Trump also appeared to gesture at others as those around him stood with hand over heart while the anthem was played. 

Information from ESPN's Dave McMenamin and The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Unbeaten Vikings' dominant defense presents an untimely test for Daniel Jones and the reeling Colts
articles.description: — Daniel Jones made a pit stop with the Minnesota Vikings two years ago, when the eighth-year quarterback got an up-close look at the
articles.headlineJa: 無敗バイキングスの強力なディフェンスが、ダニエル・ジョーンズと低迷するコルツにとって不運な試練となる
articles.descriptionJa: ダニエル・ジョーンズは2年前、ミネソタ・バイキングスに短期間滞在し、8年目のクォーターバックとして〜を間近で見た。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Daniel Jones made a pit stop with the Minnesota Vikings two years ago, when the eighth-year quarterback got an up-close look at the confusing and disruptive defense he's tasked this week with trying to solve.


              The Vikings and their league-leading pass rush will present a significant challenge for Jones and the struggling Indianapolis Colts on Sunday afternoon, with the crowd noise at U.S. Bank Stadium as an added inconvenience.


              “I saw them in practice a little bit. It’s a little different than preparing for a game and playing in a game, so we go off of what we see on film, what they’ve done this year, and then have a plan for that,” said Jones, the sixth overall pick in the 2019 draft by the New York Giants who joined the Colts last season. “But it’s a good system. There’s no question about it. They’re good with what they do. It’s different than what you see in a normal week.”


              Jones, who parlayed a standout performance at Minnesota in a wild-card round win in the 2022 postseason into a new contract valued at $160 million, was cut by the Giants halfway into the first year of that hefty extension. The Vikings snagged Jones as a backup to Sam Darnold they could also evaluate as a potential future starter.


              “Our experience with him was nothing but positive, and so to me he’s got a little bit more insight instead of some other guys as far as what we do,” said Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, whose blitz-driven group leads the NFL in several statistical categories including sacks per pass attempt. 


              “We may have to add a few wrinkles, change a few calls, that he may be privy to that some other guys aren’t.”


              When the Vikings decided not to re-sign Darnold, who went on to win the Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Vikings were banking on being able to bring Jones back to compete with J.J. McCarthy as the 2024 first-round draft pick debuted following knee surgery that wiped out his rookie season. 


              But Jones prioritized the assurance of a starting job and signed instead with the Colts, where he played well until a torn Achilles tendon in early December and a tough schedule down the stretch toppled the team's 8-2 start.


              The Colts are reeling again this season at 2-4, having fired general manager Chris Ballard at the beginning of the week.


              “It definitely makes you feel something," Jones said. "You understand kind of what’s at stake, so we know we’ve got to play better.”


              The Vikings, meanwhile, are 5-0 and refreshed from a bye week that should allow wide receiver Jordan Addison, left tackle Christian Darrisaw, tight end T.J. Hockenson, and running back Jordan Mason to return from recent injuries.

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.
articles.headlineJa: ウェイン・ルーニー：ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとマン・ユナイテッドの選手たちは「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っている
articles.descriptionJa: ウェイン・ルーニーは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのチームが「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っていると猛烈に批判し、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとリサンドロ・マルティネスに自省を促した。
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.

Fernandes followed Martínez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League.

The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martínez -- who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox -- of being selfish.

Sources: Carrick to lead Man United against Bournemouth

During an appearance on "The United Stand" podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick's future, said: "When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start.

"We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn't talk, but I'd run through a brick wall for him on the pitch.

"These players, they're selfish. They care about themselves, they don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

"If they're not getting what's right for them. They're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves.

- Ogden: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Dawson: Man United were abysmal in Como, but only Carrick who will suffer

"Bruno, he's having probably the worst run of form he's had since he's been at the club and again, it's no coincidence he's putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players... they'll find what is looking back at them is them and it's not good enough."

articles.headline: NFL Week 7 uniforms: Alternates galore as Texans go battle red, Lions all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 7, led by alternate looks from Houston, Detroit and Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第7週のユニフォーム：テキサンズのバトルレッドやライオンズのオールブラックなど、多彩なオルタネートが登場
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストン、デトロイト、ダラスのオルタネート仕様を中心に、NFL各チームが第7週に着用するユニフォームを紹介する。
articles.body:
The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions.

Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The New York Giants will counter with all-white. 

Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers. The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024. 

The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. Atlanta's threads include its iconic red helmet, which dates back to the 1960s, with black jerseys and white pants.

articles.headline: LaMelo Ball obviously traveled on way to 3-pointer, NBA refs confirm
articles.description: The association that represents NBA referees confirmed that LaMelo Ball took two steps too many and traveled in a widely seen clip from Wednesday night's win over Miami.
articles.headlineJa: ラメロ・ボールの3ポイントシュートへの動きは明らかにトラベリング、NBA審判団が確認
articles.descriptionJa: NBA審判を代表する協会は、水曜夜のマイアミ戦での勝利における広く拡散された映像の中で、ラメロ・ボールが2歩多く踏み出し、トラベリングを行ったことを認めた。
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Upon review, Minnesota's LaMelo Ball traveled.

Really, really traveled.

The association that represents NBA referees posted a clip from Wednesday night's game between the Timberwolves and the Miami Heat and clarified -- not that it needed much clarification -- that Ball indeed did commit a violation on his way to a 3-pointer in the second quarter of Minnesota's win.

"For everyone asking, 'how is this legal?' It's not!" the referees' union wrote in a post on X. "He gathers with his right foot on the floor and would be permitted two steps by rule (left-right). He takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels."

Even Ball's brother, seven-year NBA player Lonzo Ball, got the call right moments after the play.

"Travel lmaoooo," Lonzo Ball posted.

Told in an interview with ESPN after the game that his brother made the traveling call, LaMelo Ball -- who was making his Minnesota debut -- still insisted he didn't commit a violation.

"He hatin'. He hatin'," LaMelo Ball said in the televised interview. "See, I gotta give him a call right now, cause with the family, he knows what you're supposed to do. Even if I'm wrong, I'm right. That's how it goes."

Ball's shouldn't-have-counted shot broke what was a 39-39 tie at the time, but in the end it wasn't like the 3-pointer played a big role in the outcome. LaMelo Ball finished the game with 21 points, and Minnesota won 131-106.

articles.headline: Chiefs place LT Josh Simmons on IR as rehab process stalls
articles.description: The Chiefs have placed left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, further delaying his return from a bulging disk in his lower back.
articles.headlineJa: リハビリが難航、チーフスがLTジョシュ・シモンズを故障者リスト（IR）に登録
articles.descriptionJa: チーフスは、腰の椎間板ヘルニアからの復帰がさらに遅れることとなり、レフトタックルのジョシュ・シモンズを故障者リスト（IR）に登録した。
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have placed left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, further delaying his return from a bulging disk in his lower back.

Simmons, the Chiefs' first-round pick in 2025, has not played this season and has been unable to practice with his teammates since Aug. 17.

"Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day, and he improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week," head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder told reporters Thursday. "However, we feel he plateaued in the recovery process. ... He's just not there yet."

Burkholder said Simmons still doesn't need surgery as part of his recovery. The trainer said an MRI exam confirmed the herniated and bulging disk, which was "higher up than we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case."

The IR move means the earliest Simmons could play this season is Week 11 at home against the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 22.

On the right side, Jaylon Moore remains in the concussion protocol, which means Joshua Ezeudu is expected to start at that tackle position Sunday night in Seattle.

Since selecting Simmons in the draft, Kansas City has played more games without him (14) than with him (eight). The Chiefs have had Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie from Indiana, start in Simmons' absence this season.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Jets' Reich likes when star playmakers 'make noise' about targets
articles.description: When Garrett Wilson isn't getting his share of targets, Jets OC Frank Reich hears about it from coach Aaron Glenn and indirectly from the star wide receiver.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツのライヒ、スタープレーメイカーがターゲット数について「声を上げる」ことを歓迎
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツのOCフランク・ライヒは、ギャレット・ウィルソンに十分なターゲットが回ってこない際、アーロン・グレンコーチやスターワイドレシーバー本人から間接的にその状況を聞いている。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- When his star wide receiver isn't getting his share of targets, New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich hears about it from coach Aaron Glenn and, indirectly, from the man himself, Garrett Wilson.

"Garrett is the ultimate team player and the ultimate pro, and in his moments of frustration -- I'm not down on the sideline, so I don't see all of them, but I hear about them," Reich said Thursday, smiling.

"I don't mind when guys make a little bit of noise," Reich added. "I like when they make noise."

Wilson hasn't publicly complained, but it becomes a story whenever he's not involved in the offense. Such was the case last Sunday, when he was targeted only twice through three quarters in a 26-19 loss to the New England Patriots. He was visibly upset and grumbling aloud as he walked to the locker room.

He was a nonfactor in two of the Jets' four losses, putting Reich under the spotlight. It's one of several issues for Reich, whose unit ranks 25th in scoring (18.7 points per game). The Jets (2-4) face the Miami Dolphins (0-5) on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

Defending his usage of Wilson, Reich said he's not afraid to spread the ball around, though he acknowledged the objective is to get Wilson involved "as early and as often as we can." When that doesn't happen, Glenn chimes in via the headsets.

"AG's always kind of in my ear ..." Reich said. "If Garrett hasn't gotten the ball for a little bit, he's like, 'Hey, don't forget, get our playmakers the ball.' That kind of thing, which is good."

Statistically, Wilson is off to one of the best starts of his career. He's ninth in receptions (35), 14th in receiving yards (418) and 15th in targets (48). Most receivers would love those numbers. Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension last year, gets frustrated when the team loses and he's not a big part of the offense.

Wilson said he hasn't asked the coaches to come up with different ways to get him the ball.

"No, they've got it covered," he said. "They're doing everything in their power. It's just about taking advantage of what we do get ... and me having a sniper mentality. When it's a play where I have a chance to have an impact on the game, you have to be spot on. You can't miss.

"I would say they're on top of it. That's what they want. They think that's a good recipe. It's not like I'm trying to convince them that it's the right thing. They see it that way, too."

Reich said there are times when he's "comfortable" if Wilson isn't getting targets, as long as others are producing. While Wilson had only four catches for 44 yards against the Patriots, his presence probably created opportunities for rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who enjoyed a breakout with six catches for 103 yards and a touchdown.

articles.headline: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?
articles.description: The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to much more than their manager. Who deserves the most blame, and why?
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uの混乱、責任は誰にあるのか：キャリック、選手たち……それともラトクリフ？
articles.descriptionJa: ユナイテッドに関する苦い真実は、その長期化し根深い衰退の原因は監督だけではないということだ。誰が最も責められるべきであり、その理由は何か？
articles.body:
Manchester United are in crisis -- again. One of the world's biggest football clubs is in the middle of its worst start to a season in 40 years and suffered their heaviest Champions League defeat since 1994 when losing 4-1 to Como this week, so who is to blame?

Is it the owners -- the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe -- the senior executives, the manager or the players? The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to all of the above.

So why does the blame lie in all areas, and what, if anything, can be done to drag United out of its doom spiral? ESPN has assessed United's problems and why nobody at Old Trafford can escape the scrutiny for the club's cycle of failure.

- Dawson: It's dire at Man United, but only Carrick will suffer

- UCL Talking Points: What to make of Man United's mess?

- Who are Como? The vacation-destination club that just rocked Man United

The Glazers

United have been owned by the Glazer family since 2005 following the completion of a controversial leveraged buyout.

The Glazers, who also own the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, purchased United for £790 million but borrowed £600 million, using the club as security for the loan, to complete the deal. As a consequence, the previously debt-free club was instantly plunged into £600m of debt.

That debt has been a millstone for United ever since and during the 21 years of Glazer ownership, over £1 billion has gone out of the club in debt repayments, accumulated interest, refinancing costs and dividends to shareholders. Every year of Glazer ownership has seen an average of £50m go out of the club on non-football costs -- a figure that could translate into a new signing or more attractive player wages.

Under the Glazers, Old Trafford has become a decaying stadium no longer fit for purpose and the team has suffered from long-term under-investment. Although the Glazers surrendered control of football operations to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Feb 2024 -- a £1.25 billion pay-day for a 27.7% stake in the club -- the nine-year period Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement as manager in 2013 and Ratcliffe's arrival was dominated by poor managerial and executive appointments by the Glazers and a woeful player recruitment record.

Everything that is going wrong at United can be traced back to the Glazers.

Percentage of blame: 50%

Sir Jim Ratcliffe

One of Britain's richest men and a lifelong United fan born less than 10 miles from Old Trafford, Ratcliffe was billed as the club's savior when he bought a 27.7% stake in exchange for control of football operations in February 2024.

He promised to overhaul the club, saying United's data analytics department was "last century," and he made an immediate impact by hiring Man City chief operating officer Omar Berrada as CEO and recruiting director football Dan Ashworth from Newcastle. articles.headline: Ravens' Trey Hendrickson on facing Bengals: 'It's not about me'
articles.description: Ravens outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson made it clear Wednesday that he was not interested in talking about his upcoming reunion with the Bengals, sidestepping repeated questions about his first game against his former team.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンスのトレイ・ヘンドリクソン、ベンガルズ戦を前に「私個人のことではない」
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンスのアウトサイドラインバッカー、トレイ・ヘンドリクソンは水曜日、古巣ベンガルズとの再戦について語る意思がないことを明確にし、古巣との初戦に関する繰り返される質問をかわした。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson made it clear Wednesday that he was not interested in talking about his upcoming reunion with the Cincinnati Bengals, sidestepping repeated questions about his first game against his former team.

As the Ravens prepare to play the Bengals on Sunday, Hendrickson did not want to talk about what emotions he may have facing Cincinnati and chose not to directly answer a question about whether he's looking forward to sacking his former teammate Joe Burrow.

"It's not about me," Hendrickson said. "It's about the team and what I can bring and what we can collectively do as a unit."

Hendrickson, 31, signed a four-year, $112 million contract with the Ravens this offseason after four Pro Bowl seasons with the Bengals. His 61 sacks with Cincinnati from 2021-25 ranked as the fourth most in the league.

Last year, Hendrickson had a contract dispute with the Bengals that lasted throughout spring workouts and training camp. He eventually received a $14 million raise before the start of the season.

Asked if there was any bad blood with the Bengals, Hendrickson said, "As a Christian, I forgive and I move on. There are wonderful times that I had there. There will be a time to reflect on all that stuff. But right now, there's an opponent in front of us. As the Ravens, we look forward to capitalizing on everything we can."

Hendrickson broke a finger on his right hand in the third quarter of the season opener and then missed two games following surgery. He has two sacks for Baltimore this season, but his 30% pass rush win rate ranks third in the league, according to ESPN Analytics.

Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson predicts a big game from Hendrickson on Sunday.

"I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those ones, like [a] multiple-sack game," Simpson said. "I'm calling it, [and] I'm excited to see the celebration he does." Similarly, those in Cincinnati have had very little to say about facing Hendrickson again.

When asked to sum up Hendrickson's five seasons with the Bengals, Burrow had a one-word response: "Productive."

Bengals coach Zac Taylor was also limited in his comments about the former Pro Bowl edge rusher.

"He's a good player," Taylor said on Monday. "And so again, they have a lot of good players on their defense and we got to put together a great plan and be able to execute it to give ourselves the best chance to win."

Hendrickson is one of three former Bengals players to reach at least four Pro Bowls. Hendrickson and wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase were Cincinnati's only two first-team All-Pro selections in the past 10 years.

However, Hendrickson's time ended unceremoniously after a back injury that sidelined him for the bulk of last season, one that occurred following unfulfilled trade requests and the lack of a long-term extension.

But Cincinnati knows Hendrickson will be especially motivated against his former club.

articles.headline: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet activated off PUP list
articles.description: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet, who has yet to play this season after scoring 12 TDs in 2025, has been activated off the PUP list and added to the 53-man roster.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet, who has yet to play this season, has been activated off the physically unable to perform list and added to the 53-man roster on Thursday.

Charbonnet, a co-starter last season who rushed for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns alongside Kenneth Walker III, has been working his way back from February ACL surgery. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday for the first time since he returned to practice Oct. 1.

No word has been made on his playing status for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs, but coach Mike Macdonald on Monday said there was a "possibility" that he could see action "in some capacity."

"Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps, so that's exciting," Macdonald said.

In a corresponding move, the Seahawks placed tight end Elijah Arroyo on injured reserve after he suffered a shoulder injury last week against the Denver Broncos. Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Arroyo will have season-ending surgery on Thursday.

articles.headline: Erling Haaland set to return with Man City 'hungry' to continue perfect start
articles.description: Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.
articles.body:
Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available to return for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.

Haaland, who has scored 12 goals in nine games to start to the season, remained on the bench throughout Man City's 5-1 Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens on Tuesday.

- Maresca determined to help Foden back to his best

- Walker: 'No intention' of removing Man City tattoos

- Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale

But Maresca confirmed Thursday that the Norway striker is in line to return, while Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Mateo Kovacic had been improving as City prepare to visit Villa Park after three consecutive home games.

"We have a session this afternoon. [The injured players] can all be available or not in terms of still doubt," Maresca told a news conference. "Yesterday, they were all improving, and we'll see this afternoon. For sure, Erling is the only one 100% available."

City go into the game three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the Premier League, with Maresca having begun his first season in charge with seven straight league wins.

Despite the perfect start, the former Chelsea coach insisted the team is not resting on its laurels.

"The mood is very good," Maresca said. "I said many times the mood is good. We are happy with our start but we are more hungry for more wins. We're happy at the moment but want more.

"It's too early [to say teams are not in the title race]. Seven games, there are many games to go. It's too early."

As well as Haaland, Rayan Cherki has been another major contributor to the positive early weeks of Maresca's tenure. The France international has six goals and two assists thus far and Maresca praised Cherki as one of Europe's best players when deployed in the right areas.

"If we are able to keep him there, and if we are able to find him between the lines, so in the right position, I think he is one of the best player in Europe," Maresca said.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Thursday's NBA slate features just two games, both between teams with championship aspirations

LeBron James will make his home debut with the Philadelphia 76ers against a Cleveland Cavaliers team led by Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Evan Mobley. Cleveland added Peyton Watson this offseason but could be without Jarrett Allen, who is questionable for Thursday's game with a knee injury. If Allen can't play, defending Joel Embiid becomes an even bigger challenge. Philadelphia opened the season with a win over the defending champion New York Knicks on Tuesday.

The second game features Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets opening their season on the road against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder beat the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday behind 32 points from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Denver added DeMar DeRozan and Marvin Bagley III this offseason but lost the aforementioned Watson to the Cavs, leaving the Nuggets with a different bench rotation.

Let's take a closer look at both matchups and some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Fantasy stream team: Widely available players worth adding

 Aaron Gordon, PF, Nuggets (rostered in 51.6% of ESPN leagues)

Gordon averaged 16.2 PPG and 5.8 RPG in 36 games last season, providing fantasy managers with scoring, rebounds and 3-pointers. He's projected to average 29.3 MPG this season and should see enough minutes to be useful in fantasy. Gordon had 23 points and 10 rebounds in his only game against the Thunder last season.

 Jared McCain, SG/PG, Thunder (43.6%)

McCain finished with 37 fantasy points in 22 minutes against the Spurs on Tuesday. He averaged 10.4 PPG and shot 39.1% from beyond the arc after joining Oklahoma City last season. Don't expect six triples every night, but McCain should continue getting opportunities off the bench.

Moody's favorite bets for Thursday

Tyrese Maxey OVER 2.5 3-pointers (-109)

Maxey played 40 minutes against the Knicks on Tuesday, making just two of his nine 3-point attempts. He averaged 8.6 3-point attempts and 3.1 triples made per game since the 2023-24 season. Maxey should continue playing heavy minutes and has a great chance of making at least three triples tonight against a Cavaliers team that allowed one of the highest totals of 3-pointers made to guards last season.

Anfernee Simons 10+ points (+103)

Simons scored 13 points on 10 field-goal attempts in 25 minutes against the Knicks. The 76ers have several offensive playmakers, but Simons' role is clear. articles.headline: Michael Carrick set to lead Man United vs. Bournemouth amid pressure - sources
articles.description: Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.

Carrick is under mounting pressure following the disastrous 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Despite serious concerns internally about the team's form, the 45-year-old is expected to be on the touchline when United face Marco Rose's side on Sunday.

Having only signed a two-year contract in May, Carrick's long-term future remains in doubt after a run of seven games without a win and just one Premier League victory all season.

The club's hierarchy accept that if results do not turn around quickly they will be forced into a change, but there is also sympathy for Carrick's predicament.

Senior staff were left shocked at the team's performance against Como and felt that only Amad Diallo, who was introduced as a half-time substitute, emerged with any credit.

Sources have also told ESPN that there is a feeling that too many players are refusing to take personal responsibility for their own role in the team's slump.

Bruno Fernandes was substituted in the 67th minute at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium before appearing to criticise Carrick and his staff for their tactics in a post-match interview.

- Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes criticism after Man United loss

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Frank Leboeuf blasts Bruno Fernandes for 'betrayal'

The United captain is the second senior player to turn his fire on club staff in as many weeks after Lisandro Martínez directly criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

Martínez later issued a public apology and received a fine. Sources have told ESPN that Fernandes' comments will be assessed before a decision is made about whether to take any further action.

Carrick is set to hold his usual weekly news conference on Friday afternoon to preview Bournemouth's visit to Old Trafford.

United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off on Thursday, sources have told ESPN.

Information from ESPN's Mark Ogden was used in this report.

articles.headline: Soccer's main characters after UCL Matchday 3: Kane, Van Dijk, El Clasico
articles.description: Champions League Matchday 3 has come and gone, and we have some Main Character energy coming from Harry Kane, Barcelona and Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico, while Liverpool should worry about Virgil van Dijk's form.
articles.headlineJa: UCL第3節終了後のサッカー界の主役：ケイン、ファン・ダイク、エル・クラシコ
articles.descriptionJa: チャンピオンズリーグ第3節が終了した。エル・クラシコを前にハリー・ケイン、バルセロナ、レアル・マドリードが主役級の存在感を示している一方で、リヴァプールはフィルジル・ファン・ダイクのコンディションを懸念する必要があるだろう。
articles.body:
`

By the time they were going for their third straight Champions League title in 2017-18, Real Madrid had mastered the art of easing in. In 2016-17, they finished behind Borussia Dortmund in their group and constantly needed their trademarked, late-game Real Madrid magic to secure points before igniting in the knockout rounds. For the three-peat, they finished second in their group behind Tottenham Hotspur, but mostly rolled in the spring again.

Paris Saint-Germain have certainly learned that you don't have to look your sharpest early on. Two seasons ago, in their first of what is currently a two-year title streak -- and in the first year for the expanded league phase structure -- they narrowly beat Girona in their first match and then lost three of their next four matches before finally starting to click into place in December. They won their next five Champions League matches by a combined 18 goals, knocked off top-seeded Liverpool in penalties in the round of 16 and ... mostly rolled from there.

You can play with fire without getting burned, but Luis Enrique has decided he really doesn't want to. PSG started far better last year, winning four of their first five league phase matches, and this fall they've been all business: After a 6-1 tuneup against Slovan Bratislava to start, they've beaten Manchester City and Barcelona, each by multiple goals. They were winless in their first four matches in all competitions in this campaign, but when the Champions League began, so did their season.

- UCL Power Rankings: Can anyone slow PSG down?

- Talking Points: Man United's mess, PSG lose Kvara, more

- Dawson: Who are Como, the destination club making waves

Along with a 2-2 draw between Arsenal and Bayern Munich, PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona was the most noteworthy result of Champions League Matchday 3, even if Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's ACL tear cast a bit of a pall on the proceedings. But five teams continued their perfect starts -- PSG, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Real Betis -- and all of the most likely candidates to win next week's Ballon d'Or made exciting plays.

The league phase keeps rolling, but here are soccer's five main characters as we move past Matchday 3.

Main character No. 1: Harry Kane's closing argument

The voting for this year's Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded this coming Monday, closed a while ago. While the prediction market odds were shifting toward Barca's Lamine Yamal for a while, they appear to have homed in on Bayern Munich's Harry Kane as the likely winner, and justifiably so. He simply had the best year of anyone, winning three trophies, leading England to the World Cup semifinals for a second time and -- oh yeah -- scoring 73 goals with eight assists in 65 total matches. Yamal had only 25 and 20, respectively, in the same period. articles.description: Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Meanwhile, Arsenal want £55 million in any potential deal for striker Viktor Gyökeres.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martínez are playing for their futures at Old Trafford, with their contracts due to expire next summer. That's according to according to TEAMtalk, which claims that United are not rushing to make a decision on the three defenders. That comes as preparations are being put in place for potential defensive reinforcements in 2027, with center back and left back set to be the main areas of consideration.

- Chelsea are showing interest in a move for Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari, claims TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Sweden international is in talks with the Seagulls over a contract extension, with his deal expiring in the summer, though the club has the option to extend it by a further year. However, while there are hopes of sealing a long-term stay with the club, talks have stalled over an improved contract. That has brought Chelsea into the conversation, with the Blues eyeing another swoop on Brighton, while Turkish Super Lig side Galatasaray are also monitoring the situation.

- If Viktor Gyökeres does leave Arsenal in the next year, then the North London club has set a valuation of £55 million on a potential exit, reports Football Insider. That is the same amount as the initial fee the Gunners paid Sporting CP to land the striker last summer. However, after a slow start to the current campaign, the Sweden international continues to be linked with a possible move away. Clubs in Italy, Spain, and elsewhere in England are keeping track of the situation, should the 28-year-old become available.

- Arsenal are among a group of teams following a potential switch for Monza striker Gustavo Varela. That's according to Mundo Deportivo, which claims that the Gunners are joined by Napoli and the 21-year-old's former club, Benfica, in keeping track of his progress. Varela has scored eight goals in seven matches across all competitions for Monza, making an impressive start with his new club. While Benfica is keen on a return, there is no clause that could guarantee a move back to Portugal, though there is a clause that will allow for the club to match an offer accepted from another club. However, with Arsenal and Napoli in the mix, that prospect has been described as difficult.

- Liverpool are in no rush to engage in conversations with Alexis Mac Allister over a new contract, despite the player voicing his disappointment at the lack of an offer earlier this season. articles.headline: Mourinho made Real Madrid-Barcelona Clásico rivalry unmissable. Now, he's back for more
articles.description: Thirteen years after helping turn soccer's biggest rivalry into must-see chaos, Real Madrid coach José Mourinho returns to face Barcelona in El Clásico with something to prove
articles.body:
José Mourinho says he doesn't look back. In August, at his debut news conference as returning Real Madrid coach after 13 years away from LaLiga, he was asked if he'd missed the Bernabéu.

"I'm not one for regrets," he said. "I'm not one for [thinking about] bad decisions, missing things ... I'm here today, there tomorrow. I don't think much about what I've left behind."

In El Clásico, club football's most storied rivalry, Mourinho left plenty behind. In three tumultuous seasons in charge of Madrid between 2010 and 2013, he faced Barcelona 17 times in LaLiga, the Copa del Rey, the Spanish Supercopa and the UEFA Champions League.

- Watch El Clásico live, 10/25, 4 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

- Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in El Clásico

- Master of reinvention: How Raphinha transformed into Barça's star striker

For the first two years, his adversary in the Camp Nou dugout was Pep Guardiola; in the third, it was Guardiola's former assistant, Tito Vilanova. By the end, Mourinho's Clásico record read: five wins, six draws, and six defeats.

In that time, both teams delivered unprecedented 100-point seasons, their duelling stars pushing each other to new heights. In 2011-12, Lionel Messi scored a record 50 goals in LaLiga. It wasn't enough to beat Mourinho's Madrid to the title. But numbers alone cannot adequately describe that feverish period.

This was, in many ways, peak Clásico. Pep vs. José. Messi vs. Cristiano Ronaldo. It wasn't always pretty; it was sometimes downright nasty. But it was always riveting. And there, at the centre of it all, revelling in the spotlight, was Mourinho, orchestrating the chaos.

"In this [press] room, he's the f---ing boss, he's the f---ing man," an exasperated Guardiola vented in April 2011. "He's the smartest guy in the world."

Guardiola is long gone, but Mourinho is back, chosen by president Florentino Pérez as the coach to get Madrid on track after two trophyless seasons, and to tame a dressing room which proved too temperamental for predecessors Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa to handle. On Sunday, in his first Clásico in 13-and-a-half years, Mourinho has the chance to prove that despite a long absence, he was always the right man for the job.

The panorama he finds now, in 2026, isn't radically different from when Mourinho first took charge at the Bernabéu in May 2010, having just won the Champions League with Inter Milan. Then, as now, Madrid had gone two seasons without any silverware. Then, as now, Mourinho was tasked with besting a Barcelona side which was already well established, supremely confident, and expertly coached.

Guardiola had already been Barça coach for two seasons. In his first, 2009-10, he had won a historic Treble. When Mourinho arrived in the summer of 2010, Guardiola was on the way to lifting a record six trophies in the calendar year.
